nodes.title: Governance: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Governance. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of Azure Policy?
flashcards.back: Azure Policy helps enforce rules (e.g., 'all VMs must use managed disks', 'resources must be tagged') and evaluates compliance of existing resources.

flashcards.front: What is Azure Blueprints?
flashcards.back: Azure Blueprints define a repeatable set of resources that implements and follows organizational standards. Unlike ARM templates, Blueprints track deployed resources and can be updated centrally.

flashcards.front: What is an Azure Subscription?
flashcards.back: Subscriptions are billing units in Azure. Each subscription has its own billing, limits, and RBAC. Organizations often use separate subscriptions for dev, test, and production environments.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of Azure Resource Tags?
flashcards.back: Tags (e.g., 'Environment:Production', 'Owner:TeamA') enable cost reporting by department, automated policies, lifecycle management, and resource organization across subscriptions.

nodes.title: Compute: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Compute. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which Azure service provides serverless code execution?
flashcards.back: Azure Functions is a serverless compute service. You write event-driven code and pay only for execution time. No server management required.

flashcards.front: What is Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)?
flashcards.back: AKS is a managed Kubernetes service. Azure manages the control plane (API server, etcd) for free; you manage and pay for worker nodes. Integrates with Azure AD, Monitor, and Container Registry.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between Azure Scale Sets and standalone VMs?
flashcards.back: VM Scale Sets let you deploy and auto-scale a group of identical, load-balanced VMs. When demand increases, Scale Sets add VMs; when demand drops, they remove them — reducing manual management.

flashcards.front: What is Azure App Service?
flashcards.back: App Service supports .NET, Node.js, Python, PHP, Java, and containers. Azure manages patching, scaling, and infrastructure. You deploy code or containers and configure scaling rules.

flashcards.front: What is Azure Cognitive Services?
flashcards.back: Azure Cognitive Services provides pre-built AI capabilities via REST APIs: Computer Vision, Face, Speech-to-Text, Text Analytics, Translator, and more. No ML training required. speech, language, decision) that enable apps to see, hear, speak, understand, and decide without ML expertise

flashcards.front: What is Azure Machine Learning?
flashcards.back: Azure ML provides MLOps capabilities: experiment tracking, automated ML, model registry, pipelines, and deployment to real-time or batch inference endpoints. Supports Python, R, and popular ML frameworks. deploying, and managing machine learning models at scale

flashcards.front: What is Azure Cognitive Search?
flashcards.back: Azure Cognitive Search (now Azure AI Search) provides full-text search with AI enrichment pipelines. Can index documents, images, and structured data, adding semantic search, vector search, and AI-extracted metadata.

flashcards.front: What is Azure Bot Service?
flashcards.back: Azure Bot Service provides a framework for building conversational AI bots. Integrates with Azure Cognitive Services (LUIS/CLU for NLP, QnA Maker/Knowledge Base for FAQ). Deployed to multiple channels. deploying, and managing intelligent chatbots across multiple channels (Teams, Slack, web, Cortana)

nodes.title: Cloud Concepts: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Cloud Concepts. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which cloud model gives you the most control over the underlying infrastructure?
flashcards.back: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) provides VMs, storage, and networking — you control the OS, runtime, and applications. PaaS and SaaS abstract more of the infrastructure.

flashcards.front: What is a benefit of the public cloud over on-premises infrastructure?
flashcards.back: Cloud shifts IT spending from CapEx (upfront hardware) to OpEx (pay-as-you-go). You don't buy servers; you pay for services consumed. shifts to operational expenditure (OpEx)

flashcards.front: What is a Hybrid Cloud?
flashcards.back: A hybrid cloud combines on-premises or private cloud infrastructure with public cloud services, allowing data and applications to move between environments.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between Azure Public, Private, and Hybrid cloud?
flashcards.back: Public cloud: shared, multi-tenant, Microsoft-owned. Private cloud: dedicated hardware (Azure Dedicated Host) or Azure Stack Hub on-premises. Hybrid: connects both, enabling workload portability. Private: dedicated Azure Stack or on-premises. Hybrid: combination of public Azure + on-premises/private cloud connected via VPN or ExpressRoute

nodes.title: Management: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Management. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is Azure Resource Manager (ARM)?
flashcards.back: ARM is the management layer for Azure. All Azure management tools (portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDKs) go through ARM. It enables RBAC, tagging, locks, and template-based deployments.

flashcards.front: What does Azure Advisor provide?
flashcards.back: Azure Advisor analyzes your Azure usage and provides recommendations across 5 categories: reliability, security, performance, cost, and operational excellence.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of Azure Resource Groups?
flashcards.back: Resource Groups are logical containers for organizing Azure resources. Resources in a group share lifecycle management — deploy, update, or delete them together.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between Azure Portal, CLI, and PowerShell?
flashcards.back: All three management interfaces send requests to the Azure Resource Manager API. Portal: visual, good for exploration. CLI: script-friendly, cross-platform. PowerShell: powerful scripting, better for Windows admins.

nodes.title: Security: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Security. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is Azure Defender (Microsoft Defender for Cloud)?
flashcards.back: Microsoft Defender for Cloud provides unified security management and advanced threat protection. It assesses security posture and detects threats across hybrid environments.

flashcards.front: What is Azure Key Vault?
flashcards.back: Key Vault stores secrets (passwords, connection strings), encryption keys (HSM-backed), and certificates. Access is controlled via Azure AD and RBAC. Every access is logged for auditing.

flashcards.front: What is Azure Sentinel (Microsoft Sentinel)?
flashcards.back: Microsoft Sentinel collects data at cloud scale, uses ML for threat detection, provides investigation tools, and enables automated responses (playbooks). Replaces traditional on-premises SIEM.

flashcards.front: What is the Azure Security Benchmark?
flashcards.back: The Azure Security Benchmark (now Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark) provides prioritized security recommendations for Azure aligned with CIS Controls and NIST SP 800-53. Used as a baseline in Defender for Cloud.

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of Azure Monitor?
flashcards.back: Azure Monitor collects metrics and logs from resources, enables alerts and autoscale, and integrates with other tools like Application Insights and Log Analytics.

flashcards.front: What is Azure Service Health?
flashcards.back: Service Health provides three feeds: Service Issues (active incidents), Planned Maintenance (scheduled work), and Health Advisories. Customized to your subscriptions and regions with alert rules.

flashcards.front: What is Azure Monitor Metrics vs Azure Monitor Logs?
flashcards.back: Metrics: lightweight, fast, great for real-time alerts and dashboards. Logs (Log Analytics): rich query capability with KQL, long retention, can combine data from many sources (VMs, apps, security, network). requests/sec) stored for 93 days by default, near real-time, optimized for dashboards and alerts. Logs: structured/unstructured event data in Log Analytics workspace, queried with KQL

flashcards.front: A DevOps team wants a fully managed Grafana service in Azure to visualize metric?
flashcards.back: Azure Managed Grafana is a fully managed service that runs Grafana Enterprise in Azure. It integrates natively with Azure Monitor, supports Entra ID SSO, and provides workspace-level role assignments so teams can share dashboards securely.

statements.statement: What is the purpose of Azure Monitor? Collect, analyze, and act on telemetry data (metrics and logs) from Azure and on-premises
